dedupe_keys.name: asset utilisation potential of a trucking and rail intermodal hub in the st louis region 2018

description: This report by Sidra Naseer, Chris Mondy, Anna O'Shea Newton and Ray Mundy of the Center for Transportation Studies at the University of Missouri-St. Louis, sponsored by the Midwest Transportation Center (July 2018), assesses the asset utilisation potential of building a common trucking and rail intermodal hub in the St. Louis region. More than a billion tons of cargo pass through St. Louis each year, and in Missouri 45% of cargo moves by rail and 49% by truck. Coverage: industry history, transport policies and initiatives in the region, the stakeholders affected, property rights, externalities and net benefit to society, case studies of other US cities with successful intermodal development, and geospatial mapping of freight providers in the region, used to analyse a railroad and trucking hub. The main benefit identified is lower intercity transfer cost; the authors conclude that the benefits outweigh the negatives and propose an ideal hub location. Format and access: a 38-page report PDF. Licence and cost: free, with no restrictions on distribution. Caveats: the appraisal is qualitative and spatial, not a full cost-benefit calculation. The provider map and hub logic can be used to place transfer nodes in freight network flow and capacity planning models. It relates to the Twin Ports terminal study and the Freight Analysis Framework in the catalogue.
